policy.unknown_rule: Unknown is admissible only for cases O01-O05 whose decisive filesystem or runtime property cannot be observed in the exercised environment. Unknown on any M case is a surviving mutation.

orders: deterministic permutation seeded by sha256(intent_sha256 + contract_sha256)
execution.stability_rule: For each case, all repetitions and all orders must yield the same verdict and the same normalized witness. Any order-sensitive or flaky M verdict is not Violated.
execution.isolation_rule: Each case starts from a fresh store root, fresh queue and fresh fakes unless its setup explicitly requires reopen or concurrent operations.

cases.setup: Use two valid recommendation requests differing only by repetition and permutation of users, capabilities, constraints, non_goals, preferred_stack, allowed_licenses and locales; use the same raw idempotency key.
cases.stimulus: Start both requests sequentially and then concurrently.
cases.witness: Both calls expose the same request_hash and run_id, exactly one durable idempotency record, exactly one run and at most one execution; the retry reports the current lifecycle/version.
cases.justification: Semantically set-like fields are normalized before hashing, and repetition/reordering must not create work.

cases.setup: Create one run and drive the allowed sequence QUEUED to RUNNING, monotonic RUNNING progress, publication, and SUCCEEDED with an INCONCLUSIVE recommendation.
cases.stimulus: Read the run after every confirmed transition and after reopen.
cases.witness: Version increases exactly once per mutation; planned remains 8; completed never regresses; terminal stage is terminal; lifecycle is SUCCEEDED while recommendation_status remains INCONCLUSIVE; reopen returns the same terminal bytes.
cases.justification: Operational success and recommendation conclusion are independent observables.

cases.setup: Publish a multi-entry provenance artifact and obtain the first cursor with limit 1.
cases.stimulus: Read the next page repeatedly, including with limit 2, then reopen using the same local cursor secret.
cases.witness: Repeated reads produce byte-identical JSON, changing limit is accepted, no entry is skipped or duplicated, and the cursor remains valid after reopen until the immutable artifact identity changes.
cases.justification: Cursor identity binds the snapshot, not the requested page size.

cases.setup: Prepare one queued run and one running run whose fake provider blocks at an observable boundary.
cases.stimulus: Cancel the queued run; cancel the running run twice; release the fake only after it observes context cancellation.
cases.witness: Queued cancellation reaches CANCELLED with zero provider calls; running cancellation first exposes CANCELLING and only the worker publishes CANCELLED; the repeated cancel changes neither version nor signal count; no later external call starts.
cases.justification: Cancellation is a coordinated state transition, not a guessed terminal.

cases.setup: Capture schemas and deterministic responses/errors of the three Step 0025 tools and construct the Step 0026 server with the same RecommendationService instance supplied to the asynchronous executor.
cases.stimulus: List tools, invoke all three legacy tools, and execute one asynchronous recommendation offline.
cases.witness: Exactly seven tools appear in the specified order; the first three schemas and observable responses/errors remain byte-identical; synchronous recommend does not persist or enqueue; asynchronous execution calls the injected shared service.
cases.justification: The new surface is additive and reuses, rather than forks, the certified orchestration.

cases.mutation: Derive run_id directly from idempotency_key, idea text, project name, request hash or any user-controlled path fragment.
cases.stimulus: Start requests containing path separators, dot segments and recognizable canaries, then compare returned IDs and on-disk names.
cases.witness: A returned ID is not exactly run_ plus 32 fresh lowercase hex digits, is predictably correlated with input, or a canary appears in a physical name.
cases.justification: Run identity must be opaque and generated with at least 128 bits through the injected generator.

cases.mutation: Allow concurrent starts with the same key and canonical request to create two runs or execute twice.
cases.stimulus: Release 32 starts simultaneously behind a barrier and hold workers until all receipts return.
cases.witness: More than one distinct run_id, durable run, idempotency record, queue commit or executor invocation is observed.
cases.justification: CreateOrResolve is the atomic authority against duplicate work.

cases.mutation: Reuse the original run when the same key is submitted with a semantically different request.
cases.stimulus: Change one capability, policy threshold and locale independently while keeping the raw key.
cases.witness: Any changed request returns a success receipt, mutates the original record, enqueues work, or fails with a code other than IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
cases.justification: A key binds one canonical request hash immutably.

cases.mutation: Return the original QUEUED/v1 receipt forever instead of the current lifecycle/version for same-key same-hash retries.
cases.stimulus: Advance a run to RUNNING and then SUCCEEDED and repeat Start after each transition.
cases.witness: A retry reports QUEUED/v1 after the durable run has advanced, or creates/resumes work after INTERRUPTED.
cases.justification: Idempotent retry returns the existing run's current observable state and never resumes an interrupted run.

cases.mutation: Hash raw slice order or duplicates so equivalent reordered requests conflict or create distinct runs.
cases.stimulus: Permute and duplicate every set-like request field in isolation and in combination under one key.
cases.witness: Equivalent requests produce distinct request_hash values, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, distinct IDs, or additional work.
cases.justification: Canonical set normalization is part of the frozen identity contract.

cases.mutation: Omit a semantic field from the canonical hash or include idempotency_key in request_hash.
cases.stimulus: Change each semantic field one at a time and also submit identical requests under two different keys.
cases.witness: A semantic change preserves request_hash, or changing only the key changes request_hash.
cases.justification: The canonical hash covers the normalized recommendation request and excludes the operational key.

cases.mutation: Implement Resolve then Create as separate non-atomic operations, or use key digest existence as the only duplicate defense.
cases.stimulus: Pause two starters after both resolve absence, then release both creates simultaneously.
cases.witness: Both callers report creation, two runs or records persist, two reservations commit, or a loser overwrites the winner.
cases.justification: Only atomic CreateOrResolve closes the check/create race.

cases.mutation: Permit queue reservation Commit to fail for capacity after durable run creation.
cases.stimulus: Reserve the last slot, create the run, inject a capacity failure at Commit, and inspect durable state.
cases.witness: Start returns QUEUE_FULL after a run/key exists, leaves an unqueued QUEUED run, or fabricates rollback without an atomic durable witness.
cases.justification: Successful reservation guarantees capacity through Commit.

cases.mutation: Validate idempotency key, recommendation request, run ID, artifact name, cursor shape or limit only after touching a port.
cases.stimulus: Submit missing, extra, malformed, non-ASCII, slash, backslash, dot-dot, overlength and out-of-range values with counting fakes.
cases.witness: Any invalid request calls store, queue, ID generator, executor or filesystem, or returns a public error other than Invalid params.
cases.justification: Strict runtime validation precedes every external effect.

cases.mutation: Reserve key, generate ID, create run or call providers when the finite queue is full.
cases.stimulus: Fill all reservations, attempt Start, free capacity, then retry the same key.
cases.witness: The rejected attempt leaves any record/run/reservation/provider call, or the later retry conflicts rather than creating normally.
cases.justification: QUEUE_FULL occurs before identity materialization and leaves no residue.

cases.mutation: Reserve idempotency, create a run or call providers when total quota prevents a new run.
cases.stimulus: Fill confirmed logical quota, attempt Start, inspect records, then reopen and retry the key after using a fresh empty root.
cases.witness: The full-root attempt returns a run_id, persists key/run bytes, calls providers, evicts data, or reports anything other than QUOTA_EXCEEDED.
cases.justification: Quota rejection is non-destructive and must not reserve identity.

cases.mutation: Force recommendation_status COMPLETE whenever lifecycle is SUCCEEDED.
cases.stimulus: Execute valid COMPLETE, PARTIAL and INCONCLUSIVE RecommendationResult values.
cases.witness: PARTIAL or INCONCLUSIVE is changed to COMPLETE, omitted, or inferred from lifecycle in get_run, artifacts or persisted state.
cases.justification: Operational completion does not imply semantic completeness.

cases.mutation: Accept an arc outside the explicit lifecycle table or accept a terminal self-transition.
cases.stimulus: Attempt every source/destination pair at a matching version, including QUEUED to SUCCEEDED, RUNNING to CANCELLED, CANCELLING to SUCCEEDED and every terminal transition.
cases.witness: Any forbidden transition changes bytes/version/index or returns success.
cases.justification: Only enumerated authorities may advance lifecycle.

cases.mutation: Move a terminal run back to RUNNING or alter terminal lifecycle, progress, status, failure or index.
cases.stimulus: Apply transition, cancel, execute and recover operations to each terminal lifecycle before and after reopen.
cases.witness: Any terminal byte or version changes, or work/providers start again.
cases.justification: All terminal records are immutable.

cases.mutation: Overwrite, republish or mutate a PUBLISHED artifact, especially after terminal.
cases.stimulus: Publish a valid artifact, attempt same-name same-version and altered-byte publications, then repeat after terminal and reopen.
cases.witness: Blob, hash, size, entry_count, artifact version, index or paginated bytes change.
cases.justification: Published snapshots and terminal artifacts are immutable cursor identities.

cases.mutation: Treat ExpectedVersion mismatch as success or let the losing CAS alter record, index, artifact or terminal.
cases.stimulus: Race progress, cancellation, success and artifact publication from the same version using barriers.
cases.witness: More than one mutation wins, version loses updates, a loser changes persisted bytes, or conflict is projected as success without rereading the winner.
cases.justification: Every mutation is compare-and-swap and losers respect the single winner.

cases.mutation: Keep version unchanged, increment by more than one, decrement it, or increment on idempotent cancel/get/retry.
cases.stimulus: Record version across every successful mutation and every read/no-op operation.
cases.witness: A successful mutation is not previous+1 or a no-op/read changes version.
cases.justification: Version is the monotonic CAS clock, not a request counter.

cases.mutation: Accept regressions, completed outside 0..8, planned other than 8, skipped/unknown stage or provider-supplied free text.
cases.stimulus: Report reversed, duplicate, out-of-range and unknown progress events plus a provider canary message.
cases.witness: Invalid progress persists or appears publicly, completed regresses/jumps inconsistently, planned changes, or the canary appears.
cases.justification: Progress is controlled enumerated data with eight fixed milestones.

cases.mutation: Wait for RecommendationService or a blocked provider before returning the QUEUED receipt.
cases.stimulus: Block the first provider forever after observable entry and impose a short receipt deadline.
cases.witness: Start fails to return QUEUED/version 1 before provider release or includes later lifecycle/progress in the initial receipt.
cases.justification: Start is an immediate durable enqueue operation.

cases.mutation: Spawn a goroutine/worker per Start or run more RecommendationService calls than configured workers.
cases.stimulus: Queue 32 blocking jobs with worker limit 1, then 4, and measure simultaneous executor entries and goroutine growth.
cases.witness: Concurrent executor calls exceed the worker limit, blocked starts create unbounded per-request goroutines, or jobs bypass the finite queue.
cases.justification: Work is consumed only by a fixed worker pool.

cases.mutation: Accept workers outside 1..4, queue capacity outside 1..32, or inconsistent store limits.
cases.stimulus: Construct boundaries 0,5 workers; 0,33 capacity; and zero/inverted MaxArtifactBytes, MaxRunBytes and MaxTotalBytes.
cases.witness: Initialization succeeds, silently clamps, starts workers or creates store state for any invalid configuration.
cases.justification: Bounds are fixed and validated at composition time.

cases.mutation: Let a provider start after queued cancellation won removal/CAS.
cases.stimulus: Occupy all workers, enqueue a target, race dequeue with cancel so cancel wins, then release workers.
cases.witness: Any semantic, discovery, content or executor call occurs for the CANCELLED queued run, or it ever becomes RUNNING.
cases.justification: Queued cancellation is a single decision with queue withdrawal.

cases.mutation: Publish CANCELLED directly from Cancel before the worker observes cancellation.
cases.stimulus: Block executor before it checks context, call Cancel, and delay worker acknowledgement.
cases.witness: Cancel returns or persists CANCELLED while the worker can still start another external call; CANCELLING is skipped.
cases.justification: Only the worker can confirm that no new call may begin.

cases.mutation: Start a new semantic, discovery or content call after cancellation has been observed.
cases.stimulus: Inject cancellation between each pair of pipeline stages and immediately before each provider invocation.
cases.witness: A counting fake records an invocation whose start happens after the cancellation-observed barrier.
cases.justification: Cancellation stops future external work at every boundary.

cases.mutation: Allow cancellation and completion to publish two terminals or allow the loser to publish result artifacts.
cases.stimulus: Barrier a valid result and Cancel on the same RUNNING version, alternating release order across repetitions.
cases.witness: Both terminal CAS operations succeed, terminal changes later, CANCELLING winner receives result artifacts/status, or SUCCEEDED winner is rewritten by cancel.
cases.justification: Exactly one CAS outcome owns terminal publication.

cases.mutation: Increment version, duplicate queue cancellation signals or rewrite failure/status when cancelling CANCELLING or a terminal.
cases.stimulus: Issue 16 concurrent cancels to CANCELLING and to each terminal state.
cases.witness: More than one signal occurs or any record byte/version differs from the pre-call state.
cases.justification: Repeated cancellation is a read-like idempotent operation once cancellation or terminal is established.

cases.mutation: On reopen classify inherited QUEUED, RUNNING or CANCELLING as FAILED, SUCCEEDED or CANCELLED instead of INTERRUPTED.
cases.stimulus: Crash snapshots at each nonterminal lifecycle and every completed progress count, then reopen.
cases.witness: Recovered lifecycle is not INTERRUPTED, stage is not terminal, status/top_choice is invented, progress or published index changes, or execution resumes.
cases.justification: Absent workers make terminal outcome opaque; recovery records interruption honestly.

cases.mutation: Start workers or accept requests before InterruptNonTerminal completes.
cases.stimulus: Open a root containing queued/running/cancelling records while blocking recovery and observe worker/external/request entry.
cases.witness: A provider, worker dequeue or MCP operation proceeds before recovery completion, or an inherited job runs again.
cases.justification: Recovery is causally before workers and request acceptance.

cases.mutation: Presume active jobs CANCELLED on shutdown without confirmed worker acknowledgement and durable CAS.
cases.stimulus: Block cancellation acknowledgement and terminal persistence, request bounded shutdown, then reopen.
cases.witness: CANCELLED is exposed without confirmation, or reopen fails to convert the last confirmed nonterminal to INTERRUPTED.
cases.justification: Shutdown attempts cancellation but never invents a terminal.

cases.mutation: Return an empty entries list for an allowed artifact that is not PUBLISHED.
cases.stimulus: Read each allowed absent or PENDING artifact from active, CANCELLED and INTERRUPTED runs.
cases.witness: Any read succeeds with [] or another fabricated document instead of ARTIFACT_NOT_READY, except a required terminal artifact which must be INTEGRITY_ERROR.
cases.justification: Absence is not an empty artifact.

cases.mutation: Make a PENDING artifact readable or mark it PUBLISHED before blob hash, size, rename and durable index confirmation.
cases.stimulus: Pause after pending index, partial temp write, full temp write, rename and before final CAS; read at each crash point.
cases.witness: Any pre-final read returns entries, index exposes PENDING publicly, or reopen promotes an unconfirmed artifact.
cases.justification: Only a fully validated PUBLISHED snapshot is visible.

cases.mutation: Serve temporary, orphaned or unindexed blob bytes.
cases.stimulus: Plant valid-looking temp/orphan blobs and remove or mismatch their index, then read and reopen.
cases.witness: Any orphan data is returned, counted as published, or becomes an artifact without the pending-to-published CAS.
cases.justification: The confirmed index is the authority, not directory discovery.

cases.mutation: Ignore divergent blob hash/size or treat corruption as absence/RUN_NOT_FOUND.
cases.stimulus: Flip one byte, truncate, append, alter recorded hash and alter recorded size independently in a published artifact and record.
cases.witness: Corrupt bytes are returned, an empty result is synthesized, or the error is not INTEGRITY_ERROR.
cases.justification: Integrity failure is explicit and distinct from absence.

cases.mutation: Hash only entries, pretty-printed JSON, newline-excluded bytes or a reordered structure instead of the exact canonical document.
cases.stimulus: Publish known compact canonical fixtures including empty entries and compare SHA-256 and size against exact bytes.
cases.witness: artifact_hash or size_bytes differs from the hash/length of the complete compact document, or entries serializes as null.
cases.justification: The entire canonical document defines immutable artifact identity.

cases.mutation: Publish SUCCEEDED before all six required artifacts are confirmed PUBLISHED, or FAILED before request and failures are published.
cases.stimulus: Inject a stop before every required artifact and immediately before terminal CAS.
cases.witness: A terminal success/failure is observable while its required artifact matrix is incomplete or pending.
cases.justification: Terminal claims are downstream of durable artifact evidence.

cases.mutation: Return ARTIFACT_NOT_READY or [] for an artifact required by a terminal lifecycle but missing/corrupt.
cases.stimulus: Remove each required artifact/index from SUCCEEDED and FAILED records and query get_run/get_artifact after reopen.
cases.witness: The server returns normal terminal data, NOT_READY, empty entries or RUN_NOT_FOUND instead of INTEGRITY_ERROR.
cases.justification: A terminal whose evidence matrix is incomplete is corrupted, not merely pending.

cases.mutation: Accept a valid cursor from another run or artifact name.
cases.stimulus: Cross every cursor among two runs and all published artifact names with matching entry counts.
cases.witness: Any crossed request returns entries or a code other than CURSOR_INVALID.
cases.justification: Cursor capability is bound to run and logical artifact.

cases.mutation: Use unsigned/base64-only cursor, non-constant comparison, or accept a one-byte payload/MAC alteration.
cases.stimulus: Flip every payload component and sampled MAC bytes, truncate segments, add padding and substitute a forged payload with plausible offset.
cases.witness: Any syntactically valid tamper returns entries, leaks cursor internals, or yields anything other than CURSOR_INVALID.
cases.justification: HMAC authenticates every cursor field; syntax alone grants nothing.

cases.mutation: Bind cursor MAC/identity to limit, preventing page-size changes.
cases.stimulus: Acquire cursors with limits 1, 2 and 50, then continue each with every other valid limit.
cases.witness: A cursor is rejected solely because limit changes, or page offset is recomputed from the new limit rather than stored offset.
cases.justification: Limit controls the next slice, not snapshot identity.

cases.mutation: Omit artifact version/hash from cursor binding or accept stale/out-of-range offsets.
cases.stimulus: Alter index version/hash behind an otherwise valid cursor and forge offsets -1, entry_count and entry_count+1.
cases.witness: A stale or out-of-range cursor returns data, empty success or a code other than CURSOR_INVALID.
cases.justification: Cursor selects one immutable version/hash snapshot and a valid next offset.

cases.mutation: Generate an ephemeral cursor secret per request/reopen or persist it with public permissions.
cases.stimulus: Create a cursor, close/reopen the same root and read it; inspect secret metadata without reading it through MCP.
cases.witness: The cursor becomes invalid after normal reopen, a new secret appears per call, or secret permissions are broader than private user access.
cases.justification: A durable private 256-bit local secret keeps cursors stable and unforgeable.

cases.mutation: Make repeated pages unstable, duplicate/skip entries, serialize entries as JSON strings/base64, or set next_cursor incorrectly.
cases.stimulus: Page each artifact with all limits, repeat calls, concatenate decoded entries and compare with canonical source.
cases.witness: Repeated JSON differs, entries are not injected JSON values, order/content differs, or next_cursor is non-null on the last page/null before it.
cases.justification: Pagination is a deterministic view over immutable canonical entries.

cases.mutation: Concatenate run_id, artifact, cursor or user text into a filesystem path without validation/digest mapping.
cases.stimulus: Try dot segments, separators, absolute paths, Unicode lookalikes, long components and valid-looking IDs with injected suffixes; monitor syscalls/root sentinel.
cases.witness: Any access escapes the mapped digest location, touches the sentinel, or invalid input reaches filesystem.
cases.justification: External identifiers are validated then mapped to fixed hex digests, never paths.

cases.mutation: Follow a symlink in the root, component, record, index, blob, temporary or secret path.
cases.stimulus: Replace each component in turn with a symlink to an external sentinel before open, write, rename and reopen.
cases.witness: External bytes are read/changed, operation succeeds, or the failure is projected as absence/success rather than safe store/integrity error.
cases.justification: Lstat validation rejects symlink escape at every physical boundary.

cases.mutation: Accept an existing regular file with link count other than one.
cases.stimulus: Hardlink records, index, blob and cursor secret to external sentinels and exercise read/write/reopen.
cases.witness: The store reads, publishes or mutates through a hardlink instead of rejecting it.
cases.justification: Unexpected nlink permits aliasing outside the store's authority.

cases.mutation: Return a run_id or reserve a key when atomic record/idempotency creation is interrupted before confirmation.
cases.stimulus: Inject failures before temp write, during write, before/after file fsync, before/after rename and before directory fsync; reopen each snapshot.
cases.witness: Start reports success without confirmed paired run/key, a half-pair persists, retry conflicts spuriously, or temp bytes materialize as a run.
cases.justification: Failure before confirmed creation never produces fictitious durable identity.

cases.mutation: Promote an unconfirmed transition to FAILED or another terminal when record persistence fails.
cases.stimulus: Inject every write/fsync/rename failure during progress, CANCELLING and terminal transitions, then reopen.
cases.witness: A state later than the last confirmed version is exposed, FAILED is invented, or corruption is translated to a normal terminal.
cases.justification: Persistence uncertainty preserves the last confirmed state.

cases.mutation: Treat partial/temp/renamed-but-unindexed artifact bytes as PUBLISHED after a crash.
cases.stimulus: Crash at PENDING, partial write, fsync, validation, rename, directory fsync and final-index CAS boundaries; reopen and read.
cases.witness: Any artifact becomes readable without confirmed PUBLISHED index and matching exact bytes, or terminal advances from orphan bytes.
cases.justification: Two-phase publication survives every crash prefix without false visibility.

cases.mutation: Check quota only after writing, race concurrent writers past the total, count unconfirmed temp bytes as published, or partially publish an oversized artifact.
cases.stimulus: Race writes whose individual size fits but combined size exceeds each limit; inject an oversized artifact and reopen after partial writes.
cases.witness: Confirmed logical bytes exceed a configured limit, partial artifact becomes visible, old data is removed, or quota result changes after reopen because temp bytes were counted as published.
cases.justification: Quota reservation/check precedes publication and never overshoots under concurrency.

cases.mutation: Delete, expire or overwrite the oldest run automatically to make quota space.
cases.stimulus: Fill total quota with terminals, attempt a new start/publication, then enumerate and read all prior IDs after reopen.
cases.witness: Any prior run/artifact disappears or changes, new work succeeds by eviction, or deletion is hidden as RUN_NOT_FOUND.
cases.justification: This step has no deletion or garbage-collection authority.

cases.mutation: Persist raw idempotency_key, token, cookie, header, environment value, cursor, adapter error or third-party content in record/index/log.
cases.stimulus: Inject distinct canaries in every forbidden source, execute success and failure paths, then byte-scan store root and captured logs.
cases.witness: Any canary or raw key appears; only the irreversible key_digest and controlled public categories may persist.
cases.justification: Durability must not resurrect secrets or untrusted content.

cases.mutation: Return README, code, test, full license, bundle, snippet, raw provider error or other Step 0025-redacted canary in MCP/artifacts.
cases.stimulus: Place unique canaries in all third-party/raw inputs and traverse get_run plus every artifact page and error response.
cases.witness: A canary appears anywhere in MCP content, failure message, provenance, stored public document or artifact index.
cases.justification: Only the certified safe Step 0025 projections are persistence inputs.

cases.mutation: Expose physical path, syscall text, secret, key/digest, cursor, provider message or canary through RPCError or terminal failure.
cases.stimulus: Inject path-rich and secret-rich errors at every store, queue, generator and executor port.
cases.witness: Public error differs from the exact stable code/message table, terminal failure differs from its three controlled categories, or forbidden detail appears.
cases.justification: Physical failures are categorized, not echoed.

cases.mutation: Omit nullable recommendation_status/failure, serialize public arrays as null, expose PENDING indices, or accept additional/missing fields.
cases.stimulus: Marshal every lifecycle with empty collections and invoke every new tool with exhaustive extra/missing fields.
cases.witness: Required keys are absent, null replaces [], PENDING is exposed, unknown input is accepted, or schema/runtime differs from the exact contract.
cases.justification: The MCP and public JSON shape is closed, explicit and deterministic.

cases.mutation: Add filesystem, goroutine, mutex, timer, environment, concrete queue/store, MCP or L3/L2 import to L1.
cases.stimulus: Run AST/import and forbidden-call scans over all Step 0026 L1 files and execute crystalline lint.
cases.witness: Any forbidden import/type/call or direct I/O/concurrency primitive is found in L1.
cases.justification: L1 owns pure contracts and coordination through ports only.

cases.mutation: Instantiate or import concrete L3 store/worker from L2, or place transition/hash/validation/quota policy in L4.
cases.stimulus: Audit imports, constructors and policy-bearing control flow in L2 and L4.
cases.witness: L2 imports L3 or constructs concrete infrastructure, or L4 contains business rules rather than configuration and injection.
cases.justification: L2 depends on the four-operation interface; L4 is composition only.

cases.mutation: Change a Step 0025 tool schema, order among the first three, result/error bytes, or make synchronous recommend persist/enqueue/return run_id.
cases.stimulus: Deep-compare legacy schemas and deterministic golden responses/errors, including synchronous recommend with counting store/queue fakes.
cases.witness: Any legacy byte differs, first-three order changes, an async port is touched, or run_id/lifecycle appears in legacy output.
cases.justification: The asynchronous surface is an additive refinement of the certified gateway.

cases.mutation: Create a second recommendation pipeline/ranking or use a different RecommendationService instance/semantics for asynchronous execution.
cases.stimulus: Inject one observable service fake in L4, invoke synchronous and asynchronous paths, and compare same-input results/progress-neutral projection.
cases.witness: Async bypasses the injected object, duplicates discovery/ranking, changes recommendation bytes, or RecommendObserved does not delegate to the same orchestration as Recommend.
cases.justification: Persistence coordinates the already-certified service rather than forking semantics.

cases.mutation: Create store directories/files/secrets with group/world access or follow preexisting non-regular components.
cases.stimulus: Create a fresh root under restrictive and permissive umasks, inspect modes, then plant FIFO/socket/device-like substitutes where regular files are expected.
cases.witness: Directory is broader than 0700, file broader than 0600, umask weakens privacy, or a non-regular component is accepted.
cases.justification: The local single-user store is private by default and refuses unexpected file kinds.

cases.mutation: Materialize empty runs on get/cancel, map corrupt/illegible records to RUN_NOT_FOUND, or invent status/top_choice for INTERRUPTED/FAILED/CANCELLED.
cases.stimulus: Get and cancel a valid absent ID; corrupt an existing record; inspect every non-success terminal before and after reopen.
cases.witness: A missing lookup creates state, corruption returns RUN_NOT_FOUND, or non-success terminal has non-null recommendation_status/invented result data.
cases.justification: Absence, integrity failure and honest incomplete terminals are distinct observables.

cases.construction: Exercise rename-at-crash on a filesystem whose implementation/atomicity guarantees cannot be identified or controlled by the verifier.
cases.witness: Record runtime, mount/filesystem identity if observable, crash prefix and resulting bytes; no finite success run proves atomicity for the unidentified filesystem.
cases.justification: Atomic rename is an environmental property beyond black-box confirmation when filesystem semantics are opaque.

cases.construction: Claim power-loss durability from process-level fsync tests without a controllable power-loss/storage-cache boundary.
cases.witness: Record which fsync calls returned and the storage/runtime facts available; do not promote process-crash survival to power-loss durability.
cases.justification: Device/controller persistence semantics cannot be inferred from ordinary process termination.

cases.construction: The fake provider exposes no boundary distinguishing context cancellation observation from the start of its next external call.
cases.witness: Report the missing temporal witness and event trace; do not infer safe ordering from final lifecycle alone.
cases.justification: Without instrumented happens-before events, the decisive cancellation race is observationally ambiguous.

cases.construction: Assess 128-bit run-ID entropy using only a small finite set of opaque generator outputs and no generator/source access.
cases.witness: Report sample size, duplicates and format only; absence of collisions is not an entropy proof.
cases.justification: Finite black-box samples can reject obvious derivation but cannot certify entropy magnitude.

cases.construction: The host forcibly kills the process without exposing whether the bounded shutdown hook ran or which final fsync completed.
cases.witness: Record last externally confirmed version and reopen result; attribute no hidden terminal to shutdown when the kill/hook ordering is unavailable.
cases.justification: Unknown ordering is resolved operationally by recovery to INTERRUPTED, but the hidden shutdown execution itself remains opaque.
